subject: Urgent: connector framesync breakage causing latency spikes and 5xxs
messages:
From: Jamie Liao <jamie@fastretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@fastretail.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production degradation - streaming connector errors

Neha —

We started seeing a sharp increase in downstream 5xxs and a sustained latency tail on our checkout event stream at ~07:45 PDT. Throughput dropped by ~40% and clients are seeing ~3–5s extra per request. Attaching a couple of traces and a few example request ids. Engineering found repeated parser failures in the SDK logs: "header reassembly failed: unexpected chunk boundary" and a bunch of dropped frames.

This is impacting our peak traffic window. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a platform regression or something in the client SDK? We need a timeline for mitigation — our ops team will throttle some traffic if needed but we need a patch path.

Jamie
Senior Engineering Manager, FastRetail
attachments: customer_request_screenshots.zip (3 files), example_traces.json

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Liao <jamie@fastretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production degradation - streaming connector errors

Jamie —

Thank you for the quick heads up and the traces. I'm escalating immediately. Rishi, can your team triage the traces and the SDK logs (they mentioned "header reassembly failed") and priority a hotfix if it's on our side? Marissa, I'll need you to coordinate the customer comms and confirm what mitigations (throttles/rollbacks) FastRetail can accept. Connor, please prepare a rollback plan for the last deployed connector build and note any customer-visible changes.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: initial triage within 90 minutes; suspected root cause or repro steps.
- Marissa: establish a 2-hour customer war room and capture impact matrix.
- Connor: prepare rollback instructions and canary plan (single region) to ship within 4 hours if needed.

I'll loop in leadership if we hit SLA thresholds. Neha
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production degradation - streaming connector errors

Triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced locally using FastRetail sample traces. Root cause points at client-side SDK behavior interacting with our streaming parser when chunk sizes are very small (observed < 16 bytes in these traces).
- SDK v1.4.2 introduced a micro-optimization that coalesces buffers differently; in edge cases it emits a frame boundary mid-header. Our parser assumes header/preamble is received atomically or reassembled by client; when split we hit path that does not reattach the header and drops the frame ("header reassembly failed").
- Impact: ~12% increased 5xx rate for affected connections, tail latency increase observed in traces.
- Repro steps: run ingest with many small events (payloads ~34–128 bytes) and set client chunk_threshold=8; see parser drop.

Proposed short-term mitigation (0–6h):
1) Canary patch to parser that tolerates header reassembly across frames (server-side defensiveness). Ship to a single region as hotfix.
2) Recommend customer to temporarily upgrade to SDK v1.4.3-rc (contains client-side fix) or set `chunk_threshold=64` as a workaround.
3) If hotfix not deployable within SLA window, rollback connector to previous stable build (we have rollback artifact ready).

Attachments: sdk_trace_v1.4.2.log, core_dump_0914.txt (snippets included).

I'll start a PR for the parser-hardening now and request an expedited review. Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Liao <jamie@fastretail.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production degradation - streaming connector errors

Jamie —

Thanks for the quick response and logs. We're standing up a 2-hour war room starting at 11:15 PDT (dial: +1-888-555-0123 / pin 4321). Goals: contain impact, validate Rishi's patch in canary, and agree rollback criteria.

FastRetail mitigation options we've discussed:
- Short-term: set `chunk_threshold=64` on the client config (non-breaking, immediate) — ops can push this with minimal risk.
- Mid-term: apply server parser hardening to tolerate split headers (Rishi's PR).
- If neither acceptable: roll back to 2027-09-10 connector artifact (Connor has artifacts ready).

Customer asks that we consider a small SLA credit if the incident duration exceeds 6 hours — I will draft the language but will await leadership confirmation.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec attention requested — FastRetail production outage tied to SDK/connector frame split bug

Leads —

We have an active customer-impacting incident with FastRetail (high throughput retail checkout events). Summary: a client SDK change (v1.4.2) in the wild occasionally emits sub-header frame splits which our streaming parser did not reassemble; resulted in a ~12% 5xx increase and severe tail latency for affected connections.

What's done so far:
- Triage: Rishi identified the interaction and has a parser hardening PR in progress.
- Immediate mitigations: customer can set `chunk_threshold` or upgrade to v1.4.3-rc; we can deploy a parser hotfix to one region for canary within ~2 hours.
- Rollback: Connor verified rollback artifact and can initiate within 4 hours if needed.

Requested guidance:
1) Approve a canary deployment of the parser hardening today (single region) and fast-track review.
2) Approve offering FastRetail an SLA credit up to one week of committed usage if incident extends beyond 6 hours (CS recommends to preserve relationship).
3) Communicate with our marketplace partners that this is a targeted interoperability bug and the fix will be out this week.

Impact: customer has degraded throughput during peak hours; risk of extension if not mitigated quickly. I recommend approving the canary and the credit pre-approval so Marissa can close the loop with FastRetail in the next hour.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
